clue.text: Disturbing novels upset Southeast Europeans

indicators.note: disturbing the word novels throws its letters into a new order
upset in a down clue turns the abbreviation for Southeast upside down

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

explanation.surface: Some shocking fiction has caused offence among people in the Balkans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbing' rearranges NOVELS into SLOVEN; 'upset' turns SE into ES at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenes are the people of Slovenia, a nation of south-central Europe.

clue.text: Esteemed to be overpriced

explanation.surface: A respected thing turns out to cost too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means both held in affection or high regard and costly, priced too high.

clue.text: An idle stupid guy

indicators.note: stupid suggests the words an idle are muddled into a different order

explanation.surface: A lazy, dim-witted fellow is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' is the anagram signal, rearranging AN IDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel is a man's first name, and guy is informal for a man.

clue.text: Closely involved with the issue

parts.note: issue here means offspring, so the phrase describes the relationship of mother or father to their children, not engagement with a topic

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply engaged in the matter under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is an old word for children, and mothers and fathers are the people most bound up with them.

clue.text: Love is too young to know what is" Shakespeare. Sonnets

definitions.text: Love is too young to know what is" Shakespeare. Sonnets

parts.words: Love is too young to know what is" Shakespeare. Sonnets
parts.note: the clue quotes the opening line of Shakespeare's Sonnet 151 with one word left out; the solver fills the gap from memory

explanation.surface: A line from one of Shakespeare's sonnets with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: Sonnet 151 begins 'Love is too young to know what ___ is', and the missing word is the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The sonnet's line speaks of the inner moral sense of right and wrong, which youthful love has not yet learned.

clue.text: Trendy and single-so good for one's standing!

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
sole means single, only one

explanation.surface: Being fashionable and unattached is good for your social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' looks like social status, but it means standing on your feet.
explanation.definitionFit: An inner sole lines a shoe and cushions the foot as a person stands.

clue.text: Put off with a story before ten -a mistake

indicators.note: before puts the first two pieces ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

indicators.note: mistake marks the words ten and a as wrongly placed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is turned off by a tale told before ten, which was an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' is the anagram signal; the second 'a' joins 'ten' as its fodder, while the first 'a' stands as itself; 'before' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to estrange them, making them unfriendly or hostile.

clue.text: Able to bring parking into use

indicators.note: into places the parking letter inside the word for use

parts.note: to exert is to put into use or employ
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone is capable of putting a car park to good use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals that P goes inside EXERT.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is skilled, highly capable in a field.

clue.text: A horse which has the lot!

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A horse that has everything going for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a total or sum, the whole quantity.

clue.text: Article opposing queen and state

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
V stands for versus, meaning against or opposing
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece takes a stand against the monarch and the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a nation, but it is a verb: declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare or assert something firmly.

clue.text: Permission to cause a sensation

indicators.note: to cause asks the letters of permission to be worked into something new

explanation.surface: Being allowed to make a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cause' is the anagram signal on PERMISSION, which has exactly the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An impression is a feeling or effect produced on the senses or mind.

clue.text: A Continental mineral spring that's below par

parts.note: un is French for a, so a Continental a
a well can be a mineral spring, as in spa names

explanation.surface: A European spa that is not up to standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' in British usage means mainland European, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling below par means feeling slightly ill or off-colour.

clue.text: Extensive property

parts.note: extensive is read as able to extend or stretch, and property as a physical characteristic, not a large estate

explanation.surface: A large estate of land.
explanation.definitionFit: The capacity of a material to stretch and spring back is a physical quality it has.

clue.text: Retire an infirm old family servant

indicators.note: infirm means weak or unsound, so the letters of retire an are unsteady and reshuffled

explanation.surface: An elderly, frail household servant is pensioned off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infirm' rearranges RETIRE AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a long-serving servant attached to a household.

clue.text: Worker having to cast about to find a home

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for cast goes round the worker

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast
an ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer has to wander around looking for somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a verb of throwing a net or a part in a play; it means to throw, and 'about' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a crude hut or shack used as a dwelling.

clue.text: Sure, try a merger. There's money in it

indicators.note: a merger mixes things together, so the letters of sure try a are blended anew

explanation.surface: Someone urges a corporate merger because it will be profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merger' rearranges SURE TRY A.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasury is a store or department holding funds.

clue.text: Woman entering a chapel in order to pray

indicators.note: entering suggests a name going into the run of words a chapel in order

explanation.surface: A woman walks into a chapel so that she can pray.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits inside chapEL IN ORder.
explanation.definitionFit: Elinor is a female first name, as in Jane Austen's heroine Elinor Dashwood.

clue.text: Others drop control

parts.note: the rest means the others
rain is drops of water falling

explanation.surface: Other people abandon their self-discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' looks like a verb, but it supplies RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep under control.

clue.text: Like to fly — coming and going

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Birds seem made to fly, arriving and departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aswing is swinging to and fro, moving back and forth.

clue.text: Propriety requires contact with the head

parts.note: to meet is to come into contact
a ness is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: Good manners demand you meet the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a boss, but NESS is a geographical head, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Meetness is an old word for fitness or suitability, being proper.

clue.text: Ways to divide up catch

parts.note: E and N are compass directions, ways one may go

indicators.note: up in a down clue turns the word for divide so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: to part is to divide

explanation.surface: Routes are split to snare someone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the word for divide; the two compass points stand for 'Ways'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to snare or capture by trickery.

clue.text: Soldiers going into action double up

indicators.note: going into puts the soldiers inside the word for action

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit, a case
RE is the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops entering battle are bent over in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' looks like combat, but it is a lawsuit; 'going into' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To crease is to fold, bending material over on itself.

clue.text: Dog the miner endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for miner loses its final letter

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: Someone follows a mine worker relentlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like a verb, to follow; it is the definition, a sheepdog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a breed of sheepdog.

clue.text: Not moving investments to cash repository

parts.note: stocks are investments in shares
a till is a cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: Shares are converted and the money put away in a drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless.

clue.text: Coppers are so trim

parts.note: P is pence, copper coins

explanation.surface: Police officers are well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police, but means pennies, copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to trim by cutting away the edges.

clue.text: Face the cat!

explanation.surface: Someone is told to confront the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss is slang for the face (from Irish pus, mouth), and also a familiar name for a cat.

clue.text: Put right and subsequently beam

parts.note: after means subsequently, later

explanation.surface: Fix something and then smile broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' looks like a smile, but it is a roof timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is a sloping timber supporting a roof.

clue.text: Benefits and support may well be denied

parts.note: gains are benefits or advantages
aid means support or help

explanation.surface: Welfare benefits and state help may be refused.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsaid means contradicted or denied.
